facts.text: Peabody was named after philanthropist George Peabody in 1868, honoring the man born in the area.
The city’s leather industry once shipped hides worldwide, with railroad tracks crisscrossing downtown to move the goods.
In 1930, Eastman Gelatin Corporation produced gelatin for Kodak film at the former American Glue factory on Washington Street.
The Peabody Leatherworkers Museum opened in 2009 on Washington Street, celebrating the town’s rich leather‑tanning heritage.
Peabody’s Northshore Mall, opened in 1958 on former farm land owned by millionaire Elias Hasket Derby, remains one of the region’s largest shopping centers.
The Peabody Institute Library, founded in 1852 after a bequest from George Peabody, is one of the oldest public libraries in Massachusetts.
